summary: Guankong (1903–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and became a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a law degree at the University of Tokyo, studying under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute, and founded Dogen Sangha International.

Gudrun Bühnemann (b. 1955) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Münster, Bonn, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner and Michael Hahn). She held research posts at BORI, Pune, Nagoya, and Kyoto before joining UW-Madison as professor in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As of 2026, she is attested at Munich, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and IIBS.

Guilherme de Vasconcelos Abreu (1842–1907) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Coimbra and under Abel Bergaigne and Martin Haug. In 1877, he was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at the Curso Superior de Letras.

Guillaume Le Gentil (1725–1792) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the Faculté de théologie catholique de Paris and the Collège de France, and held a post at the Paris Observatory from circa 1748 to 1792.

Guillaume Oisel is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in linguistics at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2006–2013) and served as a Docente at the National University of San Marcos in 2019.
Gunapala Dharmasiri specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund (b. 1938) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and Nils Simonsson, and she held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1978 to 2005.
Gunnar Jarring (1907–2002) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and held a post there from circa 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Monash University, the University of Sydney, and Fuyan Buddhist Institute, and under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. In 2013, he is attested as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery.

Guohui Shi (b. 1958) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo, studied under several other Japanese scholars, and was a traditional student of Sheng Yen.
Gurii Stepanov (1880–1937) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Seminary and Kazan Theological Academy, where he was appointed Docent of Kalmuk in 1909.

Gurinder Singh Mann (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from BUCC, EFLU, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught at BUCC and Columbia before holding the Kundan Kaur Kapany Chair at UCSB (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga (1874–1957) studied theology at Leiden University. He was Professor of New Testament and Comparative Religion at the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944) and a docent at Utrecht University (1944–1957).
Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, and is attested in 2014 as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

Gustaf John Ramstedt (1873–1950) was a linguist and Central Asian specialist. Educated at the University of Helsinki under Otto Donner, J. N. Reuter, and Eemil Nestor Setälä, he was professor of Altaic linguistics at Helsinki (1917–1941) and served at Tokyo.

Gustav Bickell (1838–1906) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Halle and Marburg. He taught at Marburg and Giessen, was an associate professor at Münster, and held professorships of Semitic languages at Innsbruck (1874) and Vienna (1891).

Gustav Ecke (1896–1971), a sinologist and art historian, earned his PhD at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He taught at Xiamen, Tsinghua, and Fu Jen Catholic universities, later serving as curator at the Honolulu Museum of Art and Professor of Arts at UH Mānoa.

Gustav Friedrich Oehler (1812–1872) studied at Tübingen and Berlin under Ludwig Heinrich Kapff and Franz Bopp. A scholar of religious studies and Indology, he held posts at the Basel Mission, Tübingen, Schöntal Seminary, and the University of Breslau.
